name: Requiem Solace

civilization.name: The Solacean Convergence
civilization.notes: Spacefaring civilization that deliberately returned to their homeworld and sealed themselves in underground vaults approximately 6,000 years ago; cause of extinction unknown but appears voluntary

geological_features: Impact-scarred wastelands across the equatorial region
Petrified remnants of former biosphere—stone forests and fossilized seas
Glass plains from ancient cataclysm in the southern hemisphere
specific_features: Ancient alien ruins spanning three continents—cities preserved under thin atmosphere
Buried megastructure detected by seismic survey, 400 km beneath the northern pole
Signal of unknown origin broadcasting from the megastructure at 6,000-year intervals
description: Requiem Solace is a world that chose to die. Its surface is a cold, wind-scoured expanse of grey rock and thin dust, broken by the petrified stumps of forests that grew when the atmosphere was thicker and the seas were liquid. The cities are still there—three continents of them, their structures preserved with eerie fidelity by the dry, cold, nearly airless conditions. Streets, buildings, public spaces, all intact, all empty, all waiting with the patient stillness of a civilization that put everything in order before it left.

Walking through a Solacean city is walking through a monument to deliberate endings. The architecture is graceful and precise—curved walls, open courtyards designed for a sky that once held clouds, doorways proportioned for beings slightly shorter and broader than humans. Everything is clean. Not decayed, not damaged, not looted. Clean, as if the inhabitants swept the floors before they went underground. The wind moans through empty doorways with a sound that is easy to mistake for voices, and the thin atmosphere turns the sky a shade of violet that makes everything look like a bruise.

The Solacean Convergence was spacefaring. Their orbital infrastructure has long since decayed, but surface evidence confirms they possessed interstellar capability. And then, approximately 6,000 years ago, they came home. All of them. They sealed their ships, walked into underground vaults beneath the northern pole, and closed the doors. Seismic surveys have mapped the vault complex—a megastructure 400 kilometers across—but no entrance has been found. The structure emits a single signal once every 6,000 years; the most recent emission was detected in 2652, and it contained mathematical sequences that took three years to partially decode.

Requiem Solace asks the question that no one wants to answer: what would make an entire spacefaring civilization choose to end? The vaults are sealed beyond any current technology's ability to breach—not locked, but fused, as if the Solaceans melted the doors shut behind them. The decoded portions of the 6,000-year signal appear to be a warning, though whether it warns visitors away or warns of something else entirely is debated. Archaeological teams work the surface cities methodically, cataloging a culture that left everything in perfect order. The next signal emission is calculated for approximately 8,652 CE. Some researchers argue for patience. Others argue that whatever the Solaceans were running from may still be coming.
